title: SYSTEM-PROOF-01 Real Multi-Track Workflow Proof
purpose: Empirically determine whether Locaily orchestration provides measurable system-level value over a simpler local-model workflow. This is the missing thesis validation. The experiment does not assume a positive result; a null result is equally valid evidence and triggers a diagnosis gate rather than the next roadmap milestone.
problem: Locaily has implemented a system architecture (track engine, generic core capabilities, qualified routing, composed workflows) but has not demonstrated that the assembled system is better than a simpler alternative. The original project commitment was to prove one narrow workflow before expanding. That proof has not been run. This milestone executes it.

included: A real repository that Locaily has never seen used as the proof fixture (to be selected at experiment start).
Condition A: a single local qualified model receives the entire repo_review task without track decomposition.
Condition B: the same model executes each Locaily repo_review track individually in sequence.
Condition C: existing Locaily qualification/routing selects the appropriate qualified capability for each repo_review track.
All three conditions use identical input (same repository, same task requirements, same evaluation criteria).
Human-readable output for all three conditions at the same level of completeness.
Structured scoring of all metrics listed in the metrics section.
A controlled single-capability failure in Condition C to test existing fallback behavior.
A written experiment report documenting all three condition outputs, scores, and interpretation.
A thesis verdict: positive, null, or negative as defined in thesisGate.
excluded: Adding new models, capabilities, workflows, routing layers, or benchmark infrastructure unless an existing missing dependency makes the experiment impossible to run.
A fifth workflow or any workflow other than repo_review.
Expanding the model matrix beyond currently qualified models.
RESEARCH-01 DecisionCapability work or any new routing architecture.
Automatic scoring infrastructure beyond what already exists.
Any changes to the repo_review workflow definition, track contracts, or capability contracts.
Optimization of any condition — all three conditions run with current system behavior as-is.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A real repository Locaily has never processed is selected and frozen as the proof fixture before any condition runs.
Condition A (single-model baseline) completes: one local qualified model receives the full repo_review task and produces human-readable output. All metrics recorded.
Condition B (decomposed baseline) completes: the same model executes each repo_review track individually and produces human-readable output. All metrics recorded.

Condition C (Locaily orchestration) completes: existing qualification/routing selects capabilities for each track, including one controlled failure scenario that exercises existing fallback behavior. All metrics recorded.

All required metric categories are scored for all three conditions: output quality (accuracy, useful findings, unsupported findings, completeness, structured-output compliance); execution behavior (time, retries/failures, capability/model assignment); failure behavior (failure isolation, recovery quality); resource usage where already measurable by existing instrumentation.
A written experiment report documents all three condition outputs with scores, comparison, and a clearly stated thesis verdict.

The report explicitly states one of: POSITIVE (Condition C demonstrates a measurable system-level advantage over Condition A in at least one thesis-relevant dimension — reliability, structured-output compliance, failure isolation, controllability, predictable recovery, or comparable usefulness at a lower model tier); NULL (no meaningful measurable difference); or NEGATIVE (Condition C is materially worse than Condition A). Implementation success and experiment completion are NOT sufficient for a POSITIVE verdict.

If the verdict is NULL or NEGATIVE: a diagnosis document is produced identifying the most likely architectural reason. No subsequent roadmap milestone may begin until the diagnosis is reviewed and explicitly approved by JP.

outputQuality: factual accuracy (manually scored against known ground truth about the fixture repo)
useful findings (findings that correctly identify real issues or properties)
unsupported findings (findings not supported by the actual repository content)
completeness (coverage of the major areas the repo_review workflow is designed to address)
structured-output compliance (does the output conform to the expected schema/format)
executionBehavior: retries and failures (count and recovery path)
capability/model assignment per track (which model handled each step in Condition C)
failureBehavior: failure isolation (does a single track failure corrupt the rest of the output, or is it contained)
recovery quality (does the fallback path in Condition C produce a usable partial result)
resourceUsage: resource cost where already measurable by existing instrumentation (do not add new instrumentation)

thesisGate.positiveCondition: Condition C demonstrates a measurable system-level advantage over Condition A in at least one of: reliability (fewer retries/failures per run), structured-output compliance (higher rate of schema-conformant outputs), failure isolation (contained rather than cascading failures), controllability (more predictable which model/capability handles each step), predictable recovery (fallback produces usable partial output), or comparable usefulness at a lower model tier.
thesisGate.nullResult: No meaningful measurable difference between Condition A and Condition C on any thesis-relevant dimension.
thesisGate.negativeResult: Condition C is materially worse than Condition A on primary output quality or reliability metrics.
thesisGate.nullOrNegativeAction: Produce a diagnosis document. Do not start any subsequent roadmap milestone (PX6, RESEARCH-01, fifth workflow, relay proof, etc.) without explicit JP approval after reviewing the diagnosis.
